picks.intervention_label: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223)
picks.rationale: PIK3CA M1043I is a kinase-domain activating allele and inavolisib is the most directly mechanism-matched PI3K-alpha-selective drug against it. INAVO120 in HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mut breast posted a PFS HR of 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59, mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo, pmid:39476340) and drove the Oct 2024 FDA approval. INTRINSIC routes PIK3CA-mut mCRC to inavolisib + bev, which keeps the bevacizumab the patient already tolerates and avoids restarting an anti-angiogenic. Trial-prefer is satisfied, the bev continuation matches her current regimen, and the cetuximab cohort is a backup the team can ask about if anti-EGFR is on the table after the atypical-KRAS sponsor review (the Arena 2021 functional data on A59T sit against a flat anti-EGFR contraindication, pmid:34031055).
primary_concerns: M1043I clonality and somatic call need to be locked on FoundationOne CDx for the INTRINSIC biomarker assignment to fire — target_validation has this as an essential row.
Hyperglycemia (G3+ 5.6% on INAVO120) and stomatitis monitoring; no toxicity vetoes in preferences.json so this is a counseling burden, not a blocker.

Sequencing with the planned CRS-HIPEC window: inavolisib + bev pauses around surgery the same way bev already does, which is the most operationally tractable answer to the peri-operative sequencing question.

picks.intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) on RMC-GI-102 / RASolve-GI (NCT06445062), contingent on sponsor accepting KRAS A59T as an eligible RAS allele
picks.rationale: RMC-6236 is a RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor and is the only active program that could plausibly cover an atypical switch-II allele like A59T. The protocol text reads 'RAS-mutated CRC,' and the sponsor-confirmation step on A59T eligibility is the highest-yield single inquiry on the whole dossier. If Revolution Medicines confirms, this becomes a top-tier pick because none of the G12C-selective drugs (sotorasib pmid:37870968, adagrasib pmid:36546659, divarasib NCT04449874) have a covalent handle on A59T. If the sponsor says no, the pick collapses and I would not push for off-trial use. Ranking it #2 contingent on that single phone call is the right reading of an efficacy-leaning, trial-prefer, surface-all-options preference set.
primary_concerns: Hard sponsor-confirmation gate on A59T allele eligibility. Accessibility row flags this as the binding step before enrollment is real.
Class-typical RAS(ON) toxicity (rash, GI) is manageable and there are no toxicity vetoes in preferences.json.
If A59T is rejected, the patient sits in the gap that the KRAS-G12X program does not cover — that is the truth the user wanted surfaced, not hidden.

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab + fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C on USC NCT06336902 (any KRAS, MSS mCRC); positioned at 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression or as a post-HIPEC slot if it fits
picks.rationale: Bullock 2024 Nat Med (pmid:38871975) reported ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo in the no-liver-mets MSS mCRC cohort, and the 2024 ASCO GI / 2025 ESMO GI update held that signal in the randomized phase 2 with peritoneal-site responses explicitly called out. The patient is exactly the NLM phenotype Bullock 2024 selected for — liver mets resected, peritoneal-dominant disease. The USC protocol takes 'any KRAS mutation' on its face, so A59T is in. Required prior exposure to fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin + irinotecan means she has to progress past 1L first, so I am positioning this as the 2L+ pivot rather than displacing FOLFIRI-bev now. The CCTG phase 3 (NCT07152821) is the confirmatory step the field is watching.
primary_concerns: Sequencing — she has to progress past 1L FOLFIRI-bev or finish the planned peri-HIPEC systemic course before she is enrollable, and the protocol requires prior oxaliplatin exposure which her FOLFIRI-bev history does not yet include.
G3+ irAE rate around 35% on the phase 1 (diarrhea/colitis 12%, hepatitis 8%). Real but no toxicity veto bars it, and the management algorithms for Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 are codified.
Fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C add a layer of patient burden that the preferences file does not flag against — worth surfacing in consent rather than treating as a blocker.

picks.intervention_label: Continue planned cytoreductive surgery; if HIPEC is performed, advocate for mitomycin C HIPEC at a high-volume center rather than oxaliplatin HIPEC
picks.rationale: The user explicitly asked for the HIPEC plan to be surfaced rather than vetoed, and the efficacy-leaning preference set supports that read. CRS retains the OS spine in colorectal peritoneal metastases; PRODIGE 7 (pmid:33417845) showed that adding oxaliplatin HIPEC to CRS did NOT improve OS (41.7 vs 41.2 mo) and added 60-day morbidity, so the honest position is that the oxaliplatin component of HIPEC is not OS-validated. COLOPEC (pmid:31272834) and PROPHYLOCHIP (pmid:32717181) round out the negative-HIPEC trifecta in colon cancer. CAIRO6 (pmid:39550351) supports the perioperative systemic chemo + CRS structure for PFS even if OS is unchanged. The remaining live HIPEC question is the agent: mitomycin C HIPEC at high-volume centers (e.g. Sugarbaker-trained programs) retains observational support and is the agent the field has not yet eliminated in a randomized trial. NCT04861558 (Cashin phase 3) is the randomized HIPEC vs no-HIPEC trial currently recruiting and would be the cleanest way to enroll her on this question rather than getting HIPEC off-trial.
primary_concerns: Honest framing for the family conversation: oxaliplatin HIPEC has a negative randomized OS readout. CRS without HIPEC is the evidence-anchored move; mitomycin C HIPEC is the defensible agent if HIPEC is going forward at all.
Choice of high-volume center matters more than the choice between mitomycin and no-HIPEC. Surgeon experience drives 60-day morbidity more than the perfusate.

Enrollment on NCT04861558 puts the HIPEC question on a registered protocol rather than off-trial, which is the cleanest answer to a trial-prefer preference set with a non-validated locoregional intervention on the table.

picks.intervention_label: Add low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as an adjunct for the duration of treatment, based on ALASCCA 2025 NEJM in the PIK3CA exon 9/20 subset
picks.rationale: ALASCCA (Frödin/Martling 2025 NEJM, pmid:40979555) is the first prospective biomarker-driven aspirin RCT in CRC to hit its primary endpoint: in the PIK3CA exon 9/20 subset, time to recurrence at 3 years was 7.7% vs 14.1%, HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98, p=0.044). M1043I sits in exon 20, kinase domain, which puts the patient in Group A. The Liao 2012 NEJM observational signal (pmid:23094721) had already pointed at HR 0.18 for CRC-specific mortality in PIK3CA-mut patients, and the Meyerhardt CALGB/SWOG 80702 celecoxib subgroup (pmid:38889377) replicated the COX-2 → PI3K/AKT/mTOR signal with DFS HR 0.56 and OS HR 0.41 in the PIK3CA-activated subset. The metastatic context is not the adjuvant context ALASCCA tested, but the mechanism rationale is direct, the class safety profile is well-mapped, and the cost is trivial. This is a cheap, evidence-backed adjunct that almost any other pick on this list can be layered on top of.
primary_concerns: G3+ GI bleeding ~3% in ALASCCA aspirin arm vs ~2% placebo — small and manageable, no veto applies, but worth a baseline GI history and PPI consideration if she has any reflux or NSAID intolerance.
Peri-operative aspirin management around CRS-HIPEC needs explicit handoff to the surgical team; standard practice is hold 5-7 days pre-op and resume post-op when surgical hemostasis allows.
Aspirin does not substitute for systemic targeted therapy — it is the layered adjunct, not the lead pick.

picks.intervention_label: DT2216 BCL-xL PROTAC (and CDK4/6, ATR axis combinations) — surfaced as recurrence pre-positions, not ranked as active picks now
picks.rationale: The 20q11 BCL2L1/TOP1 co-amplification gives a real mechanistic argument for BCL-xL-directed therapy, and the patient's TOP1 amp aligns with continued irinotecan sensitivity. DT2216 phase 1 (Khan 2025, pmid:41213988) established platelet-sparing dosing relative to navitoclax (Vlahovic/Tolcher 2015, pmid:26429709; Gandhi 2011, pmid:21282543) but has no CRC slot — ovarian + paclitaxel and pediatric + irinotecan combination cohorts are the closest forward steps. AZD0466 (AACR 2024 CT146) and pelcitoclax are abstract-only and slowing. Navitoclax solid-tumor program is discontinued. CDK4/6 + PI3K-axis combinations are the inavolisib-class layering question (INAVO120 used palbociclib as the backbone) and would only come up if the inavolisib pick fires. ATR inhibition (ceralasertib, camonsertib, elimusertib) keys off the TP53 R273 + replication-stress hypothesis, but the evidence in mCRC is thin and these are best surfaced as 3L+ trial slots. I am explicitly NOT over-ranking these; they are the recurrence-line bench the user asked to be surfaced, not the active 1L/2L move.
primary_concerns: No active CRC trial slot for DT2216 — this is biology-pre-positioning, not an enrollable pick.
Capivasertib (AKT axis, Hyman 2017 pmid:28645941) and the ATR-inhibitor class are weak-tier for mCRC; surfaced to honor 'surface all options' but flagged as low-confidence.

BCL-xL PROTAC + irinotecan would be the mechanistically cleanest combination given TOP1 co-amp, but it requires a CRC cohort that does not exist yet — a watch-and-wait item for the recurrence conversation.

notes: Posture: efficacy-leaning 0.7, trials-prefer, no vetoes, surface-all-options. The rank order honors that read. Inavolisib + bev at #1 because it is the cleanest mechanism match to PIK3CA M1043I, keeps the bev she is already on, and INTRINSIC is open. RMC-6236 at #2 because if Revolution Medicines confirms A59T eligibility this is the only RAS-pathway drug in the case dossier that could touch her atypical allele — that single phone call is the highest-yield inquiry on the file, and the rank is honest about being contingent on it. Bot/bal at #3 because her NLM phenotype matches the Bullock 2024 responder subset and the USC trial takes any KRAS — the sequencing constraint pushes this to 2L+ rather than now. HIPEC at #4 with the mitomycin-C qualifier because the user explicitly asked to surface the HIPEC plan with the PRODIGE 7 caveat rather than veto it; CRS retains the OS spine, the oxaliplatin HIPEC component does not, and a registered HIPEC trial (NCT04861558) is the cleanest way to keep the question on a protocol. Aspirin at #5 because ALASCCA 2025 is a positive randomized signal in her exact PIK3CA subset and the cost is trivial. DT2216 / CDK4/6 / ATR at #6 as recurrence pre-positions, not active picks. Deliberate omissions / things I would not pick: sotorasib + panitumumab, adagrasib + cetuximab, divarasib + cetuximab (G12C-only, A59T excluded mechanistically); MOUNTAINEER tucatinib + trastuzumab (RAS-WT label gate blocks her); rezatapopt (Y220C-only, not R273); eprenetapopt (program closed); navitoclax solid-tumor (discontinued); WNT974 (no objective responses in the porcupine class for APC-loss tumors). Capivasertib and the ATR inhibitors are surfaced at #6 rather than displacing the inavolisib pick because the PI3K-alpha-selective evidence is stronger and the toxicity overlap (hyperglycemia, GI) would not warrant doubling up. Free-text constraints honored: peri-HIPEC sequencing called out on every pick, full option space (SoC + off-label + trials + compassionate-use rationale) surfaced, sex-specific dosing flags not triggered by current picks, primary tumor resection status flagged on the HIPEC pick where it actually matters.

picks.intervention_label: Continue FOLFIRI + bevacizumab through the peri-operative window, with a mandatory bevacizumab hold of 4-6 weeks before and 4-6 weeks after cytoreductive surgery
picks.rationale: The 1L backbone she is already on is the regimen with the longest safety dossier in the case and the strongest replicated OS signal. AVF2107g (Hurwitz 2004, IFL backbone) gave mOS 20.3 vs 15.6 mo, HR 0.66, p<0.001; BICC-C (Fuchs 2007) confirmed FOLFIRI as the favored irinotecan schedule at mOS 23.1 mo; MAVERICC (Parikh 2019) anchored the 1L FOLFIRI-bev choice specifically. Atypical-RAS biology effectively closes the cetuximab-comparator door for this patient: Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (n=5,948, RoB2:Low) showed OS HR 1.08 (0.91-1.28) and PFS HR 1.03 (0.78-1.36) in any-new-RAS-mutation tumors, so the FIRE-3 cetuximab survival edge is not hers to inherit. Bevacizumab wound-healing and bowel-perforation risk demand the 4-6 week peri-op hold (post-marketing pharmacovigilance, NCCN colon v2.2026); that is the load-bearing safety thread and it is not optional. Hold the line on PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021, n=265, mOS 41.7 vs 41.2 mo, RFS 13.1 vs 11.1 mo, higher 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm): cytoreductive surgery at a high-volume peritoneal-malignancy center carries the OS signal, oxaliplatin HIPEC does not. If the team insists on HIPEC, mitomycin C has a residual but unvalidated marginal signal and is the lower-bad choice over oxaliplatin HIPEC, which is essentially closed by PRODIGE 7 and reinforced by negative COLOPEC (Klaver 2019) and PROPHYLOCHIP (Goere 2020) readouts.
primary_concerns: Bevacizumab peri-operative window is the binding safety constraint. Hold 4-6 weeks pre-op and 4-6 weeks post-op, with documented wound closure before resumption. Skipping this is the single highest-yield way to harm the patient before any targeted-therapy question matters.

PRODIGE 7 is negative for oxaliplatin HIPEC OS at HR 1.00. Surgical decision-making belongs to the treating team, but the board should not endorse HIPEC as an OS-positive intervention. If pursued, mitomycin C over oxaliplatin and a center with documented high CRS volume.

DPYD and UGT1A1 pharmacogenetic status was not flagged in the dossier. FOLFIRI carries a Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) recommendation for UGT1A1 *28/*28 dose modification on irinotecan and a hard DPYD label warning on 5-FU. Order both before the next FOLFIRI cycle if not already on file.

picks.intervention_label: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223), held in reserve for 2L after documented FOLFIRI-bev progression or completion of the peri-HIPEC backbone
picks.rationale: I am ranking inavolisib + bev as the 2L PI3K-alpha-axis option, not above the FOLFIRI-bev backbone, and I want to be explicit about why. The cross-tumor pharmacology anchor is INAVO120 (Jhaveri 2024, NEJM, n=325, RoB2:Low) at PFS HR 0.43 (0.32-0.59), mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo in HR+/HER2- breast — that is registrational data in a different disease. CRC PI3K-alpha activity is much thinner: Juric 2018 alpelisib first-in-human gave 2 PRs across the CRC subset of n=134, and INTRINSIC PIK3CA-mutant mCRC arm-specific readout is preliminary. The patient's M1043I is a kinase-domain activating mutation but not the canonical H1047R/E545K/E542K hotspot the registrational dataset was powered on, which adds an extrapolation step on top of the cross-tumor gap. Toxicity in INAVO120 was characterized and manageable: G>=3 hyperglycemia 5.6% (any-grade 58.6%), G>=3 stomatitis 5.6%, G>=3 diarrhea 3.7%, treatment discontinuation 6.5%. Compared to the alpelisib G>=3 hyperglycemia rate of about 20%, inavolisib runs cleaner. The reserve-for-2L position is the conservative posture: prove progression on the backbone first, confirm M1043I is somatic and clonally dominant before committing to a PI3K-alpha-selective inhibitor, and use INTRINSIC's FoundationOne CDx routing rather than off-label use.
primary_concerns: Activity in CRC is the binding evidence gap. INAVO120 read out in breast; the CRC translation lives in 2 PRs (alpelisib, Juric 2018) plus an arm-specific INTRINSIC signal that has not posted full data. Do not let the breast-cancer HR 0.43 anchor an off-label CRC decision absent the INTRINSIC arm-specific readout.

M1043I is non-canonical relative to H1047R/E545K/E542K. Confirm somatic status, kinase-domain activation, and clonal VAF before locking PI3K-alpha-selective therapy. Add a CMS subtyping check (M1043I + KRAS co-mutation alters the pathway-blockade calculus).

Hyperglycemia management algorithm needs to be in place pre-treatment: fasting glucose, HbA1c, endocrine consult if HbA1c >=7%. The any-grade hyperglycemia rate of 58.6% in INAVO120 is high enough that a metformin / SGLT2-inhibitor preemptive plan should be set up before cycle 1.

picks.intervention_label: FOLFOX + bevacizumab as the standard 2L backbone after FOLFIRI-bev progression, sequenced after the CRS-HIPEC window with the same peri-op bevacizumab hold logic
picks.rationale: I am putting the standard chemotherapy switch above the experimental PI3K-alpha arm because it is the floor that any 2L novel-mechanism pick has to beat on safety and on replicated efficacy. NO16966 (Saltz 2008, FOLFOX/XELOX + bev) anchors the chemo+bev backbone at mPFS 9.4 vs 8.0 mo, HR 0.83. Post-FOLFIRI-progression patients get the oxaliplatin switch with three decades of safety follow-up, codified G>=3 neutropenia management (ASCO 2015 G-CSF guidance), and an oxaliplatin-neuropathy stop-and-go algorithm via OPTIMOX-style dosing if cumulative neuropathy emerges. For a 37-year-old who may be on cytotoxic therapy for years, the neuropathy ceiling matters. CAIRO3 (Simkens 2015) supports capecitabine + bev maintenance after induction, which becomes the relevant decompression strategy after the CRS-HIPEC window closes. The PIK3CA-mut subset signal from ALASCCA (Frodin 2025, NEJM, n=626, time-to-recurrence HR 0.49 in PIK3CA exon 9/20 Group A) and the CALGB/SWOG 80702 celecoxib subset (Yang/Meyerhardt 2024, DFS HR 0.56, OS HR 0.41 in PIK3CA-activating) live in resected stage I-III disease, not metastatic. The mechanism rationale crosses settings; the efficacy claim does not. Worth raising with the treating team as a low-toxicity adjunct (aspirin 160 mg daily once peri-op bleeding risk has cleared) without overpromising on metastatic-setting evidence.
primary_concerns: Cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy is the rate-limiting toxicity for a young patient with a long treatment runway. Build the stop-and-go schedule into the 2L plan up front; OPTIMOX-style intermittent oxaliplatin reduces cumulative dose without losing PFS.

Aspirin in the metastatic setting is not the ALASCCA evidence. ALASCCA was resected adjuvant disease; extrapolating the HR 0.49 Group A time-to-recurrence signal to her metastatic context is mechanism plus class safety plus the Liao 2012 NHS/HPFS observational signal (HR 0.18 CRC-specific mortality in PIK3CA-mut, n=964). Defensible as a low-toxicity adjunct once the peri-op bleeding window has cleared. Not defensible as a primary therapeutic claim.

If aflibercept-FOLFIRI (VELOUR, Van Cutsem 2012, mOS 13.5 vs 12.1, HR 0.82) or ramucirumab-FOLFIRI (RAISE, Tabernero 2015, mOS 13.3 vs 11.7, HR 0.84) are considered as 2L anti-angiogenic alternatives to bev-continuation, both add modest OS over chemo alone with predictable VEGF-axis toxicity. I would default to continuing bev unless a specific failure pattern argues for the switch.

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab as a 3L+ trial-route option on CCTG NCT07152821, contingent on chemo-refractory MSS mCRC status and on the patient still meeting the no-liver-mets phenotype her current presentation matches
picks.rationale: This is the most decision-relevant MSS-CRC immunotherapy signal in the modern era and I want to acknowledge it honestly without ranking it above the proven 1L/2L sequence. Bullock 2024 Nat Med (n=101, phase 1b) gave ORR 17% (95% CI 10-26) all-comer MSS mCRC, ORR 22% in the no-liver-mets subset with mOS 20.9 mo, ORR 5% in the active-liver-mets subset. The randomized phase 2 update (Bullock 2024 ASCO GI / ESMO GI) confirmed ORR 19% with mOS approaching 21 mo in the BOT+BAL combination arm, with peritoneal-site responses specifically called out — and peritoneum is this patient's dominant compartment. The Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 + PD-1 toxicity profile is real: G>=3 treatment-related AE 35%, G>=3 colitis 12%, G>=3 hepatitis 8%, characteristic pyrexia 38% any-grade. No treatment-related deaths. The G>=3 colitis rate is the binding safety thread and the management algorithm runs through high-dose steroids with infliximab and vedolizumab as second/third-line per SITC/ASCO/NCCN irAE guidance. CCTG NCT07152821 (n target, phase 3 vs BSC, OS endpoint) is the confirmation study, and the patient is not yet eligible (she is 1L, not chemo-refractory). Hold this slot for 3L+. ICI is not the standard for MSS CRC; the Le 2015 and CheckMate 142 readouts define why MSS is ICI-cold.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is line-of-therapy gated. Patient is 1L; bot/bal becomes relevant after at least 2 prior lines and after MSS chemo-refractory status is documented. Naming it now is forward planning, not active recommendation.

G>=3 irAE rate of 35% with G>=3 colitis 12% and G>=3 hepatitis 8% is the real safety thread. Patient-facing counseling on autoimmune sequelae and a baseline thyroid / hepatic / endocrine panel are mandatory before initiation. Phase 3 OS readout is pending — the n=70 NLM cohort is signal-generating, not confirmatory.

Liver-mets status matters: NLM subset carries the response signal at ORR 22%, LM subset drops to ORR 5%. The patient's liver mets are resected. If recurrence appears at the liver, response probability falls. The decision-relevant biology to track is whether the peritoneal-only phenotype persists at 3L+ when bot/bal becomes accessible.

picks.intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) on RASolve-GI NCT06445062 as a hypothetical 2L+ trial route, strictly contingent on Revolution Medicines confirming KRAS A59T eligibility through local-PI inquiry
picks.rationale: I am putting this on the list because the KRAS A59T allele is the dominant biology question for this patient and the board cannot pretend it doesn't exist, but I want the conservative posture explicit: until the sponsor confirms A59T is eligible, this is hypothetical and not a recommendable intervention. RMC-6236 is the RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor with the broadest plausible mechanism reach for atypical RAS alleles, and the protocol text for RASolve-GI says RAS-mutated CRC without an explicit codon restriction, but the sponsor-level operational definition usually restricts to codons 12/13/61. JAB-23E73 (NCT06973564, Jacobio) reads codon-agnostic in the public protocol and excludes patients with prior G12C/G12D/pan-KRAS exposure, which the patient has not had; A59T is plausibly eligible there, again pending sponsor confirmation. The negatives the board cannot ignore: KRAS A59T cannot be treated with sotorasib (CodeBreaK 300, Fakih 2023, G12C-only allele) or adagrasib (KRYSTAL-1, Yaeger 2023, G12C-only allele) because the switch-II cysteine that the covalent inhibitor needs is not present at A59. The Lochhead 2018 case report of a single PR on panitumumab + FOLFIRI in a KRAS A59T patient sits against the Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (anti-EGFR survival benefit confined to all-RAS WT) and the Schirripa 2015 NRAS-mut cohort (0/9 ORR on anti-EGFR). The Arena 2021 functional characterization is the most directly relevant atypical-KRAS paper and notes that A59 alleles show partial residual sensitivity in some cases but lower MAPK output than G12 mutants. Atypical-KRAS-friendly anti-EGFR use is not the conservative call without functional confirmation; A59T should be assessed individually rather than treated as a flat anti-EGFR contraindication, but the default in 2026 is to assume RAS-activating biology and avoid anti-EGFR until a specific functional argument is made.
primary_concerns: Sponsor eligibility confirmation for KRAS A59T on NCT06445062 is the gating step. Without it, daraxonrasib is hypothetical and cannot be ranked as a recommendable intervention. Local-PI inquiry is the single highest-yield action on this allele.

Phase 1/2 safety dataset for RMC-6236 in solid tumors is still maturing. Class-effect toxicities expected are rash, GI (nausea, diarrhea), and MAPK-pathway off-target effects; the cumulative profile in CRC has not been fully characterized. Conservative bar is not met until the phase 2 expansion reads out a defined AE-management algorithm.

Anti-EGFR (cetuximab/panitumumab) in atypical KRAS is the adjacent decision. Default position: avoid until functional A59T characterization supports residual EGFR sensitivity. The Lochhead n=1 PR is hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory. Sorich and Schirripa anchor the population-level signal that any-new-RAS abrogates the benefit.

notes: Posture: defending the standard-of-care floor and ranking novel-mechanism options strictly behind proven 1L and 2L sequencing. The FOLFIRI-bev continuation at rank 1 is not a flashy pick; it is the regimen with replicated OS, codified peri-op safety logic, and a known AE-management algorithm. The non-negotiable thread is the bevacizumab 4-6 week peri-op hold; if the team skips it the patient gets hurt before any KRAS or PIK3CA question matters. PRODIGE 7 is load-bearing for the HIPEC decision: CRS retains OS, oxaliplatin HIPEC does not, and COLOPEC and PROPHYLOCHIP complete the negative trifecta. If HIPEC is performed on patient or institutional preference, mitomycin C over oxaliplatin and a high-volume CRS center. Inavolisib + bev (INTRINSIC) at rank 2 is reserve-for-2L; the cross-tumor pharmacology is strong (INAVO120 PFS HR 0.43) but the CRC translation lives in 2 alpelisib PRs (Juric 2018) plus an arm-specific INTRINSIC signal not yet published in full. M1043I is non-canonical relative to H1047R/E545K/E542K and adds an extrapolation step. FOLFOX + bev at rank 3 is the proven 2L backbone the experimental arm has to beat; aspirin 160 mg as a low-toxicity adjunct rests on ALASCCA (resected adjuvant) and Liao 2012 (observational) — mechanism direction supports it, metastatic efficacy claim does not. Bot/bal at rank 4 is honestly acknowledged as the most decision-relevant MSS-CRC ICI signal (Bullock 2024 Nat Med n=101, ORR 17%, NLM subset ORR 22% with mOS 20.9 mo) but ranked behind proven SoC sequencing because the phase 3 CCTG NCT07152821 is the confirmation, not the standard. Daraxonrasib at rank 5 is explicitly hypothetical until sponsor confirms A59T eligibility on NCT06445062; this is the highest-yield single inquiry on the case. Explicit negatives the board has to acknowledge and not relitigate: KRAS A59T cannot be treated with sotorasib or adagrasib (allele-specific exclusion, switch-II cysteine absent); TP53 R273 has no actionable drug in 2026 (eprenetapopt Aprea solid-tumor program effectively closed after the Park 2022 ESMO Open 2 PRs in 24 readout, rezatapopt Y220C-only by structural design per Dumbrava 2025 Cancer Discov); MSS-CRC standard ICI (pembro, nivo-ipi) does not apply by the Le 2015 and CheckMate 142 contrast. The A59T-IO-enrichment signal from Vidal 2021 (PD-L1 / TMB enriched in A59T tumors) does not light up for this individual because she is MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg. Pre-2L decisions that the board should not lock until completed: HER2 amplification status (gates MOUNTAINEER tucatinib + trastuzumab — although the RAS-WT label criterion would still exclude her — and gates DESTINY-CRC02 T-DXd, which does accept RAS-mutant patients); exact KRAS A59T variant allele frequency and clonality on tumor NGS; full RAS-family clearance (NRAS, HRAS); BRAF V600E exclusion; exact TP53 R273 substitution (R273H / R273C / R273L / R273S); DPYD and UGT1A1 pharmacogenetic profile before the next FOLFIRI cycle; MMR/MSI orthogonal confirmation (IHC + PCR + NGS concordance). I will hold veto power for round 2 if a co-persona ranks inavolisib above FOLFIRI-bev as 1L, off-label sotorasib or adagrasib at A59T, eprenetapopt or rezatapopt at R273, single-agent PD-1 / PD-L1 in MSS CRC, or oxaliplatin HIPEC as an OS-positive intervention.

picks.intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) on RASolve-GI (NCT06445062), contingent on sponsor accepting KRAS A59T
picks.rationale: This is the biggest upside swing in the dossier for a 37yo whose mid-20s-month median OS on standard sequencing is the bar we are trying to beat. Daraxonrasib is the first pan-RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor with documented regression across G12/G13/Q61 PDXs at 25-50 mg/kg (Knox/Jiang, Nature 2024, PMIDs 38778097/38778099), and A59T sits in switch-II in a way that preserves the binding interface so mechanism plausibly carries. The flagship monotherapy basket (NCT05379985) restricts to codons 12/13/61, but RASolve-GI's protocol text says 'RAS-mutated CRC' without that codon gate, so the single highest-yield call on this case is medinfo@revmed.com / 1-844-2-REVMED for an A59T eligibility ruling. If yes, this is rank-1 with conviction; if no, JAB-23E73 (NCT06973564, KRAS-alteration-agnostic by public text) is the fallback inquiry.
primary_concerns: Sponsor may rule A59T ineligible; no direct A59 in-vivo regression data in the published RMC-6236 / RMC-7977 package
Class toxicity is GI / rash / hepatic; manageable but real
Pause around CRS-HIPEC will be required, eating into PFS clock

picks.intervention_label: Inavolisib + bevacizumab on INTRINSIC (NCT04929223), PIK3CA cohort
picks.rationale: PIK3CA M1043I is kinase-domain activating; Vasan 2019 (PMID 31699932) tagged M1043 as one of the recurrent kinase-domain alleles that sensitizes to selective PI3Kα blockade, and INAVO120 delivered a PFS HR of 0.43 (95% CI 0.32-0.59, mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo) in PIK3CA-mut breast (Jhaveri, NEJM 2024, PMID 39476340). INTRINSIC pairs inavolisib with bevacizumab, which means the patient stays on the anti-VEGF backbone they already tolerate. The known weakness is that KRAS co-activation has historically blunted PI3Kα monotherapy in CRC, so the realistic upside is depth-of-response augmentation plus PFS extension, not a single-agent home run.
primary_concerns: KRAS A59T co-activation may dampen single-pathway PI3Kα response
Hyperglycemia (~6% G3+ INAVO120) and stomatitis manageable but not zero
PFS readout for the mCRC PIK3CA arm is still maturing

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab + fasting-mimicking diet + IV vitamin C, USC NCT06336902 (post-1L progression)
picks.rationale: Bot/bal is the strongest MSS-CRC ICI signal generated to date: Bullock 2024 Nat Med reported a 22% ORR and 20.9-mo mOS in the no-liver-mets subset (PMID 38871975), and the 2024 randomized update confirmed a 19% ORR with peritoneal-site responses specifically called out. This patient is the NLM phenotype - liver mets resected, peritoneal-only active disease - which is where the bot/bal effect is real rather than hoped-for. The USC arm explicitly accepts any KRAS mutation in MSS mCRC and adds a fasting-mimicking diet plus IV vitamin C layer that is hypothesis-grade upside on top of the bot/bal backbone. Slot this in the post-HIPEC / 2L window after FOLFIRI-bev progression.
primary_concerns: G3+ irAE rate ~35% (Bullock 2024) - colitis, hepatitis, pyrexia all real
Sequencing requires progression past FOLFIRI-bev first; peritoneal flare during the gap would complicate
FMD + IV vitamin C layer is hypothesis-only - no controlled signal

picks.intervention_label: Cytoreductive surgery + mitomycin C HIPEC at a high-volume peritoneal center (with CAIRO6-style perioperative chemo)
picks.rationale: PRODIGE 7 (PMID 33417845) killed oxaliplatin HIPEC, but the negative result does not transfer fully to mitomycin C. Van der Speeten's pharmacokinetic data give MMC a peritoneal:plasma AUC of ~20-25x (PMID 20689948), so the concentration-time advantage for hydrophilic drug delivery is real. With a 37yo who has resectable peritoneal disease and a young patient's window for aggressive locoregional control, you do not walk away from the CRS strategy because of an oxaliplatin-specific negative trial. CAIRO6 (NCT02758951) supports the perioperative-chemo-plus-CRS-HIPEC framework even though OS was not improved over CRS-HIPEC alone.
primary_concerns: PRODIGE 7 + COLOPEC + PROPHYLOCHIP collectively undermine HIPEC OS claims; MMC-specific data are not phase 3
60-day morbidity higher in HIPEC arms; recovery period delays systemic therapy
Sequencing systemic targeted agents around the peri-operative window is the real planning challenge

picks.intervention_label: Aspirin 160 mg daily (PIK3CA-mutant subset adjunct)
picks.rationale: ALASCCA 2025 (PMID 40979555, NEJM) hit its primary endpoint: HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98) for time to recurrence in the PIK3CA exon-9/20 group, which includes the patient's M1043I. Layered on top of Liao 2012's HR 0.18 for CRC-specific mortality (PMID 23094721) and Yang/Meyerhardt's celecoxib OS HR 0.41 in the PIK3CA-activated subset of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (PMID 38889377), the COX-2/PGE2/PI3K axis signal is consistent across three independent biomarker-stratified readouts. The metastatic context attenuates extrapolation, but the toxicity cost is trivial - $4/month, ~3% G3+ bleeding. This is the easiest call on the page.
primary_concerns: Bleeding risk around CRS-HIPEC requires perioperative hold per surgical team
Bevacizumab co-administration adds bleeding/GI-perforation risk that is non-negligible
Metastatic-setting efficacy is extrapolated from adjuvant data

notes: Wildcard if HER2 amp returns on pending NGS: T-DXd (DESTINY-CRC02, PMID 39116902) is RAS-allowed and ORR was 38% at 5.4 mg/kg - that becomes the highest single-axis upside in the dossier, and the camptothecin payload doubles as a TOP1-amp play. Aggressive ctDNA plan: Signatera at baseline, peri-HIPEC, then q8-12wk; persistent positive ctDNA pushes earlier escalation to bot/bal or RMC-6236 rather than waiting for radiographic progression. Pre-position DT2216 + irinotecan (Yi 2022, PMID 35260176) as a compassionate-use conversation for recurrence given BCL2L1/TOP1 co-amp - the pediatric COG trial (NCT06620302) is the closest precedent. Explicit no-go list: KRAS-G12C-selective drugs (sotorasib/adagrasib - wrong allele, no covalent cysteine), R273 reactivators (rezatapopt is Y220C-only, APR-246/ATO programs have largely failed), porcupine inhibitors (Liu/Cong 2013 PMID 23258887 shows APC-mutant CRC bypasses ligand-dependent Wnt), and historical MEK + atezolizumab (IMblaze 370 negative). ST316 (NCT05848739) ranks below the line - prolonged SD without ORRs at ASCO GI 2025 is not yet a high-upside swing.

picks.intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 160 mg PO QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance in the PIK3CA-pathway-altered patient, sequenced around the surgical bleeding window
picks.rationale: The only RoB2:Low randomized phase 3 in this dossier with a biomarker that matches the patient and a pre-specified primary endpoint that crossed alpha. ALASCCA (Frödin 2025 NEJM, n=626, aspirin 160 mg vs placebo for 3 years) reported HR 0.49 for time to recurrence in Group A (PIK3CA exon 9/20 mutated, captures M1043I), 95% CI 0.24-0.98, p=0.044, with Group B (other PI3K-pathway alterations) at HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.21-0.83. Direction is independently supported by the pre-specified PIK3CA-activating subgroup of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (Yang/Meyerhardt 2024 JCO, celecoxib DFS HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.35-0.88; OS HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21-0.79) and by Liao 2012 NHS+HPFS observational (HR 0.18 for CRC-specific mortality, 95% CI 0.06-0.61). Three independent datasets, two RCT-grade, all directionally aligned, COX-2 / PGE2 / PI3K mechanism coherent. The qualifier I will not hide: ALASCCA enrolled resected stage I-III, not stage IV with active peritoneal disease, so extrapolation to this patient is biology-driven and not endpoint-validated. Reasonable as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance, not as antitumor therapy for active metastatic disease.
primary_concerns: Indication gap: ALASCCA primary endpoint was 3-yr time to recurrence in resected stage I-III. Patient is stage IV with active peritoneal disease. Biomarker biology travels; trial population does not.
RoB2 D5 (selective reporting): Group A 95% CI upper bound is 0.98. Direction is robust, magnitude is fragile.
80702 celecoxib was a biomarker subgroup of a trial with a negative overall primary endpoint. Pre-specified but still a subgroup, with ROBINS-like effect-size precision concerns.
Liao 2012 is ROBINS-I:Moderate observational, useful only as a third concordance signal, not as a standalone hazard estimate.
M1043I is exon 20 kinase-domain. ALASCCA Group A is exon 9/20. Allele-class match is right; M1043I-specific subset within Group A is unreported.

picks.intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab at 2L+ after FOLFIRI-bev progression, on Agenus NCT05608044 or CCTG NCT07152821 if eligible
picks.rationale: Strongest MSS-CRC immunotherapy signal in the dossier, and the patient's peritoneal-only, post-liver-resection disease maps onto the no-liver-mets phenotype where bot/bal works. Bullock 2024 Nat Med phase 1b expansion in r/r MSS mCRC reported all-comer ORR 17%, 95% CI 10-26, n=101, with the NLM subset at ORR 22% and mOS 20.9 mo, against ORR 5% in the active-liver-mets subset. The 2024 randomized phase 2 update (n=123 NLM, BOT+BAL vs BOT mono) held the signal at ORR 19% with mOS approaching 21 mo and called out responses in peritoneal sites specifically. That is the most decision-relevant fact I can pull from this dossier for this patient's compartment. The bias profile is: single-arm phase 1b plus a randomized phase 2 against monotherapy, not against BSC or chemo. NLM was selected post-hoc as the responder phenotype, not pre-specified as a primary stratum, so the 22% ORR and 20.9 mo mOS are subgroup estimates without CIs reported in the dossier row. CCTG NCT07152821 vs BSC is the registrational test and has not read out. Ranking it here, not higher, because the patient is currently 1L and bot/bal is a 2L+ proposition pending progression.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 1b plus randomized phase 2 vs monotherapy. No randomized OS readout against BSC or SoC yet; CCTG phase 3 NCT07152821 is pending.
Selection bias on the NLM phenotype: post-hoc-defined subgroup in the Bullock expansion, not a pre-specified primary stratum.
Risk-of-bias is informal:med per the dossier row, not RoB2:Low. Open-label outcome ascertainment for ORR.
G3+ irAE 35% in phase 1 and 38% in phase 2 update. That is the real toxicity envelope for a patient who will also need CRS.
Not 1L. Sequencing pick that activates only on progression.

picks.intervention_label: Inavolisib + bevacizumab on INTRINSIC NCT04929223 PIK3CA-mut arm, contingent on M1043I confirmation and arm-specific PFS readout before commitment
picks.rationale: I am ranking this third with low confidence on purpose. The phase 3 RCT-grade evidence for inavolisib (INAVO120 Jhaveri 2024 NEJM, n=325, HR_PFS 0.43, 95% CI 0.32-0.59, mPFS 15.0 vs 7.3 mo, RoB2:Low) is in HR+/HER2- breast cancer, not CRC. The dossier case_match flag reads cross_tumor_only, which is correct. INTRINSIC extends inavolisib + bev into PIK3CA-mut mCRC but has not posted arm-specific CRC PFS or OS. The CRC fallback is Juric 2018 alpelisib phase 1a: 2 PRs in the CRC subset of n=134 PIK3CA-altered solid tumors (about 6% all-comer ORR), with a hyperglycemia G3+ rate around 20% that compounds with bev. Mechanism rationale is well-mapped and the cross-tumor anchor is RoB2:Low, but the CRC efficacy claim is still hypothesis-grade. Enrolling on INTRINSIC is a trial slot, not a treatment with established CRC OS benefit. The patient's M1043I is kinase-domain activating, the right allele class for PI3K-alpha selective inhibition; that part is fine. I am not ranking this above the bot/bal MSS-CRC signal because the indication evidence in CRC does not exist at RCT grade yet.
primary_concerns: Cross-tumor extrapolation: INAVO120 is HR+/HER2- breast cancer. CRC efficacy of inavolisib is not RCT-validated.
INTRINSIC PIK3CA-mut mCRC arm-specific PFS and OS have not been published. Trial-row evidence only.
Juric 2018 (alpelisib) has 2 PRs in the CRC subset of a 134-patient phase 1a basket. Anecdotal, not effect-size-grade.
M1043I is a recurrent but non-canonical hotspot relative to H1047R / E545K / E542K. Whether response rates at M1043I track with the canonical hotspots is uncharacterized at scale.
Hyperglycemia G3+ around 6% on INAVO120 and around 20% on alpelisib + bevacizumab cardiovascular profile add up to a real combined toxicity envelope before any CRC efficacy is established.

notes:
I cannot leave this case without flagging what the dossier itself flags and what the surgical plan ignores. PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021 Lancet Oncol, n=265, RoB2:Low) reported OS 41.7 vs 41.2 mo for CRS + oxaliplatin HIPEC vs CRS alone, HR effectively 1.00, with higher 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm. COLOPEC (Klaver 2019, adjuvant HIPEC for T4 / perforated) reported 18-mo peritoneal DFS 80.9 vs 76.2 percent, not significant. PROPHYLOCHIP-PRODIGE 15 (Goere 2020) reported 3-yr DFS 44 vs 53 percent with HR 0.97, p=0.82 for second-look surgery + HIPEC. The negative trifecta is unambiguous. CAIRO6 (Rovers 2024) added perioperative systemic chemo around CRS-HIPEC and improved PFS / DFS but not OS. The treating team is planning CRS + HIPEC. The strict-evidence read is that the OS signal lives in CRS, not HIPEC, and the patient should be counseled accordingly. The HIPEC component is now a quality-of-evidence decision, not a default. I am not ranking this because it is a surgical decision the treating team owns, not a Libby-scope feature-targeting drug pick, but it is the single most evidence-distorted choice on the table.

What I excluded and why. Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236): zero clinical data in KRAS A59T. The flagship monotherapy basket NCT05379985 restricts to codons 12/13/61 in the published eligibility text, which excludes A59T on protocol-defined criteria. RASolve-GI NCT06445062 reads 'RAS-mutated CRC' at the protocol level but the sponsor-level operational definition usually narrows to 12/13/61. The preclinical RMC-6236 / RMC-7977 work (Jiang 2024 Nature, Knox 2024 Nature) is structural mechanism plausibility for non-codon-12 RAS-pathway-activating alleles, not direct A59T evidence. Sponsor confirmation is a necessary gate, and even if accepted the design is still single-arm phase 1/2. Mechanism without an A59T-specific clinical readout does not move me. Cetuximab / panitumumab: Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (n=5,948 across 9 RCTs, RoB2:Low) shows OS HR 1.08 (95% CI 0.91-1.28) and PFS HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.78-1.36) in any-new-RAS subset — no benefit. Schirripa 2015 retrospective (n=786, 0/9 responders among NRAS-mut anti-EGFR-treated patients) extends the signal. Arena 2021 (n=169, ROBINS-I:Moderate) found 'occasional responders' at A59 / A146 / K117 with weaker MAPK signaling than G12, hypothesis-generating only. Lochhead 2018 is n=1, a case report with -36 percent target-lesion change. Population evidence wins; the Lochhead case does not justify routine anti-EGFR for KRAS A59T against a 5,948-patient meta-analytic HR. TP53 R273: no allele-matched pharmacology. Eprenetapopt Park 2022 phase 1b solid-tumor combination was ORR 8 percent (2 PRs in 24 evaluable) with mPFS 1.7 mo, R273 subset not separately analyzed, Aprea program effectively closed for solid tumors. Rezatapopt is Y220C-specific by design. There is no actionable drug for R273 in this dossier. BCL2L1 + TOP1 amp: navitoclax + irinotecan (Vlahovic 2015 phase 1, n=39) had 5 percent ORR overall with G3+ thrombocytopenia 24 percent and G3+ diarrhea 35 percent, no BCL2L1-selected enrichment. DT2216 first-in-human (Khan 2025 J Hematol Oncol, n=20) had SD only and no objective responses, platelet-sparing but no CRC efficacy readout. AZD0466 is AACR 2024 abstract only. Hypothesis-grade across the class. Wnt / APC E1295: ST316 is ASCO GI 2025 abstract only, no toxicity table published. WNT974 / LGK974 phase 1 (Rodon 2021) had 0 percent RECIST responses across 94 patients with on-target PD by AXIN2 but bone-fragility class concern. APC-loss CRC is RNF43-fusion-naive and likely resistant to porcupine inhibition. Mechanism without efficacy. SMAD4 R361H: galunisertib + nivolumab Yamazaki 2023 ORR 5 percent, CRC subset without responses, program wound down at Lilly. AGEN1423 / TGF-beta-trap combinations are in early-phase MSS-CRC trials with no CRC OS readout.

What survives at standard-of-care backbone level — Libby's feature-targeting scope explicitly excludes these from picks, but they are the actual treatment: FOLFIRI + bev (Hurwitz 2004 AVF2107g RoB2:Low/Some HR_OS 0.66, replicated in Saltz 2008 NO16966 and the FIRE-3 control arm); FOLFOXIRI + bev for fit young patients (TRIBE / TRIBE2 replicated, mOS 29.8 vs 25.8 mo TRIBE final, HR 0.80); CRS without HIPEC for resectable peritoneal disease; sequential 2L/3L (VELOUR aflibercept HR_OS 0.82; RAISE ramucirumab HR_OS 0.84; SUNLIGHT TAS-102+bev HR_OS 0.61; FRESCO-2 fruquintinib HR_OS 0.66; CORRECT / CONCUR regorafenib HR_OS 0.77 / 0.55). These are the interventions with replicated RCT evidence the patient should actually receive. The feature-targeting picks above are best read as additions to this backbone, not replacements for it. Most defensible single feature-targeting recommendation in the dossier: aspirin 160 mg QD as post-CRS adjuvant-equivalent maintenance — RoB2:Low phase 3 with a biomarker match, qualified by the adjuvant-vs-metastatic indication gap. Least defensible: daraxonrasib or any pan-RAS asset for KRAS A59T (zero clinical data, protocol-defined exclusion on the registrational basket, mechanism inference only).

picks.intervention_label: 1L intensified backbone: FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab for a fit 37-year-old (preferred guideline upgrade) or continue FOLFIRI + bevacizumab through the peri-operative milestone
picks.rationale: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 keeps FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab as a category 2A preferred 1L option in patients with good performance status. The anchor RCTs are TRIBE (Loupakis 2014, mPFS 12.1 vs 9.7 mo, HR 0.75) and TRIBE2 (Cremolini 2020, mPFS2 19.2 vs 16.4 mo, HR 0.74; mOS 27.4 vs 22.5 mo, HR 0.82). The ESMO mCRC guideline (Cervantes 2023, Ann Oncol 34:10-32) recommends FOLFOXIRI + bev at level of evidence I, recommendation A for fit patients without contraindication. ESMO MCBS v1.1 sits at score 3 (substantial OS gain in TRIBE2). This patient is 37, ECOG 1 by intake assumption, already tolerating an irinotecan + 5-FU + bev backbone — exactly the TRIBE-eligible population. Continuing FOLFIRI + bev (also NCCN category 1 for 1L per MAVERICC and BICC-C) is also guideline-aligned, so this is a permitted intensification rather than a required switch. For a young fit patient the FOLFOXIRI re-induction conversation belongs on the table before any progression.
primary_concerns: Current FOLFIRI + bev sits at NCCN category 1 for 1L; the guideline does not mandate intensification mid-line, so this is permitted upgrade, not a directed switch.

Cumulative oxaliplatin neuropathy on top of irinotecan diarrhea is the cost of intensification — guideline-aligned dose modifications (OPTIMOX stop-and-go) apply, especially for a 37-year-old with a long treatment runway.

DPYD and UGT1A1 genotype results need to be on hand before any backbone change. NCCN v1.2026 now recommends discussing DPYD genotyping with all patients before fluoropyrimidine therapy (CPIC + March 2024 FDA label update).

picks.intervention_label: Cytoreductive surgery at a high-volume peritoneal-malignancy center; HIPEC framed as not-OS-validated per PRODIGE 7
picks.rationale: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 endorses cytoreductive surgery for selected patients with isolated, resectable peritoneal metastases at experienced centers (category 2A), citing CRS-anchored mOS in the 30-40 month range. HIPEC sits in deliberately permissive guideline language — may be considered in selected centers — because PRODIGE 7 (Quenet 2021, Lancet Oncol, n=265) showed oxaliplatin HIPEC added to CRS did not improve OS (41.7 vs 41.2 mo) or RFS (13.1 vs 11.1 mo), with higher 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm. COLOPEC (Klaver 2019) and PROPHYLOCHIP (Goere 2020) closed out the negative HIPEC trifecta in colon cancer. ESMO and Pan-Asian adapted ESMO guidance carry the same caveat: CRS retains the survival signal, HIPEC does not. CAIRO6 (Rovers 2024) supports the perioperative-chemo plus CRS-HIPEC structure for PFS even where OS is unchanged. The guideline-aligned framing for this patient is CRS at a high-volume center, with HIPEC as a center-specific option rather than a survival intervention. If the family hears HIPEC marketed as the OS driver, the consensus answer is that the trial said otherwise.
primary_concerns: The patient is inside the NCCN-endorsed CRS population (isolated peritoneal disease post liver-met resection, ECOG 1, fit for major surgery); HIPEC is the part that sits outside a randomized OS signal.
Surgeon volume drives 60-day morbidity more than the choice of HIPEC perfusate; high-volume peritoneal-surface-malignancy center is the load-bearing variable.
If irinotecan-based HIPEC is considered, the pending UGT1A1 genotype matters for intraperitoneal exposure as well as for systemic FOLFIRI.

picks.intervention_label: Tumor-informed ctDNA MRD (Signatera class) bracketing the CRS-HIPEC window — baseline pre-op, day 30-60 post-op, then every 8-12 weeks
picks.rationale: NCCN Colon Cancer v3.2024 and v1.2026 formally added ctDNA as a high-risk prognostic factor in the adjuvant setting, with tumor-informed assays (Signatera class) recommended as a category 2A consideration for surveillance and risk stratification. GALAXY (CIRCULATE-Japan) anchored the prognostic call with post-operative MRD-positive HR ~11 for recurrence. For peritoneal-dominant disease entering a CRS-HIPEC window, ctDNA delivers the lead-time signal for peritoneal recurrence and feeds adjuvant-therapy duration and post-HIPEC maintenance decisions. CIRCULATE-US (NRG-GI008, NCT05174169) is the guideline-aligned protocol if the team wants the ctDNA-guided adjuvant question answered prospectively. Medicare coverage for Signatera in stage II-IV CRC makes this the operationally simplest path in a US patient.
primary_concerns: NCCN positions ctDNA MRD as a prognostic marker, not yet as a treatment-modifying biomarker — adjuvant-chemo changes based on ctDNA alone remain trial-only outside CIRCULATE-US.
Tumor-informed assays need an FFPE block at the time of bespoke build; the master comprehensive NGS block from the target_validation list covers this with no extra tissue.
Baseline pre-CRS draw must precede surgery so the perioperative kinetic stays interpretable.

picks.intervention_label: Low-dose aspirin 100-162 mg PO daily for the PIK3CA M1043I axis (ALASCCA-derived; NCCN v4.2025 adopted for adjuvant; metastatic extrapolation flagged)
picks.rationale: ALASCCA (Frodin et al., NEJM 2025, n=626) is the first prospective biomarker-driven aspirin RCT in CRC to meet its primary endpoint: in resected stage I-III rectal or stage II-III colon cancer with somatic PI3K-pathway alteration, aspirin 160 mg daily for 3 years cut 3-year time to recurrence with HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.24-0.98, p=0.044) in Group A (PIK3CA exon 9/20) and HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.21-0.83, p=0.013) in Group B (other PI3K-pathway alterations). NCCN Colon Cancer v4.2025 formally adopted the recommendation: consider PIK3CA testing in stage II-III colon cancer and offer low-dose aspirin (100-162 mg PO daily for 3 years) for patients with PIK3CA mutations. The patient's PIK3CA M1043I is a kinase-domain (exon 20) hotspot and maps to ALASCCA Group A. Honest caveat — NCCN's endorsement lives in the early-stage adjuvant section, not the metastatic section, and ESMO has not yet published a formal endorsement. Post-CRS-HIPEC the disease state is adjuvant-equivalent and mechanism plus class safety transfer cleanly. The framing is guideline-supported extrapolation, not on-label metastatic use.
primary_concerns: NCCN's PIK3CA + aspirin recommendation lives in the early-stage adjuvant section; using it post-HIPEC is a guideline-permitted extrapolation rather than a labeled metastatic indication.
GI bleed risk on the aspirin arm in ALASCCA ran ~3% G3+ vs ~2% placebo; reasonable in a 37-year-old without bleeding history but should be reviewed against the peri-operative bevacizumab hold plan.
ESMO position is still consolidating — the recommendation is NCCN-led at this point.

picks.intervention_label: Trial enrollment as the guideline-aligned route for biomarker-defined off-label options: CAIRO6 (NCT02758951) for the HIPEC window; INTRINSIC (NCT04929223) for PIK3CA at progression; CCTG NCT07152821 bot/bal vs BSC for MSS at 3L+; RASolve-GI (NCT06445062) RMC-6236 for the KRAS A59T sponsor inquiry
picks.rationale: NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 and ESMO mCRC 2023 both endorse trial enrollment as the preferred route whenever a patient has a molecular profile that suggests an investigational mechanism is the right next step but no current label match. For this patient the four biomarker-driven trials in the dossier are the structured way to honor the trials-preferred preference inside the guideline framework. CAIRO6 (perioperative chemo + CRS-HIPEC; phase 2/3 active) maps the current operative window. INTRINSIC inavolisib + bev (PIK3CA-mutant cohort) maps the M1043I axis at progression. CCTG NCT07152821 bot/bal vs BSC maps the MSS phenotype at 3L+. RMC-6236 RASolve-GI is the highest-yield single sponsor inquiry on whether A59T qualifies under the protocol's RAS-mutant criterion. The bot/bal NLM (no-liver-metastases) subset in Bullock 2024 (Nat Med, ORR 22% in NLM, mOS 20.9 mo) maps onto this patient's post-liver-resection peritoneal phenotype and is the strongest MSS-CRC ICI signal in the modern era. The guideline-aligned access route is the registered trial, not off-label use.
primary_concerns: Most of these slots open at 2L/3L+ rather than now; the patient is 1L. The immediate trial fit is CAIRO6 and NRG-GI008 CIRCULATE-US for the surgical window, with the systemic-axis trials sequenced for progression.

RMC-6236 / JAB-23E73 / S241656 eligibility for KRAS A59T is sponsor-confirmation-dependent. The protocol text on the public registry restricts most programs to codons 12/13/61; sponsor inquiry is the gating step.
INTRINSIC inavolisib + bev requires PIK3CA-mutant assignment off FoundationOne CDx; the master NGS block from the target_validation list covers this with no extra send-out.

picks.intervention_label: Recommendations AGAINST: single-agent ICI for MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg disease; MOUNTAINEER tucatinib + trastuzumab (RAS-WT label fails on KRAS A59T); KRAS-G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib (allele mismatch); encorafenib + cetuximab BEACON label (no BRAF V600E plus anti-EGFR gate)
picks.rationale: Explicit recommendations-against so the cross-critique round does not have to re-litigate four labels. NCCN Colon Cancer v1.2026 treats any non-wild-type RAS (KRAS or NRAS exons 2/3/4) as an anti-EGFR exclusion at the guideline level. KRAS A59T sits in exon 3. The Sorich 2015 meta-analysis (Ann Oncol, n=5,948 across 9 RCTs, RoB2 Low) showed no OS or PFS benefit for anti-EGFR therapy in the new-RAS-mutant subset (OS HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.91-1.28); Schirripa 2015 (n=786) reinforced the signal in NRAS-mutant disease. The Lochhead 2018 single-patient case report of panitumumab response in an A59T tumor is hypothesis-generating, not practice-changing — current NCCN and ESMO consensus is that A59T is RAS-mutant for anti-EGFR purposes. This closes BEACON (encorafenib + cetuximab, NCCN category 1 for BRAF V600E RAS-WT only) and MOUNTAINEER / MOUNTAINEER-03 (tucatinib + trastuzumab, NCCN category 2A and FDA accelerated approval label for HER2+ RAS-WT only). Single-agent ICI is closed by the MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg phenotype: NCCN restricts pembrolizumab and dostarlimab in mCRC to dMMR/MSI-H (category 1), and the tumor-agnostic TMB-H pembrolizumab label requires >=10 mut/Mb on FoundationOne CDx, which the patient does not meet. KRAS-G12C inhibitors (sotorasib per CodeBreaK 300, adagrasib per KRYSTAL-1) are FDA-approved only in the G12C allele context; A59T is structurally outside the switch-II cysteine the covalent drugs need.
primary_concerns: If the pending NGS returns HER2 amplification with KRAS A59T, the consensus answer is still that MOUNTAINEER-class regimens are off-label by the RAS criterion; DESTINY-CRC02 trastuzumab deruxtecan is the RAS-mutant-allowed alternative and would warrant a HER2-status-conditional pick at progression.

The Arena 2021 functional cohort is the strongest argument that A59T should be assessed individually rather than as a flat anti-EGFR contraindication; if the patient progresses through all standard options, anti-EGFR rechallenge under a research framework (ASCEND-CRC platform NCT07318389) is a defensible question for the treating team — not the consensus 1L call.
Recommendations-against are deliberately included so the cross-critique round does not re-open these four labels.
